description: Elderly diabetic patient with multiple medications and a critical DDI
raw_text: 65-year-old male presenting with fatigue and dizziness. Past medical history significant for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus diagnosed 10 years ago, Atrial Fibrillation, and Hypertension. Current medications include Metformin 1000mg twice daily, Glipizide 5mg once daily in the morning, and Warfarin 5mg daily (started 3 months ago for AF). Patient reports no known drug allergies. Recent labs show HbA1c 7.8%, Creatinine 1.8 mg/dL (elevated), eGFR 38 mL/min, INR 3.2 (above therapeutic range), Potassium 4.9 mEq/L. Blood pressure today: 155/95 mmHg.

expected_ddi.reason: Warfarin may enhance hypoglycemic effect of sulfonylureas

expected_flags: Metformin use with eGFR < 45 requires dose reduction or discontinuation
INR 3.2 is above therapeutic range — bleeding risk
Uncontrolled hypertension (155/95) despite no antihypertensive medication listed

description: Complex polypharmacy case with multiple moderate DDIs and misspelled drug names
raw_text: 71-year-old male with COPD, Type 2 Diabetes, depression, and chronic back pain. Medications: Glucophage 500mg BID (for diabetes), Advil 400mg TID for back pain, Zoloft 100mg daily (for depression), Lasix 40mg daily, Lisinopril 20mg daily. Allergic to Penicillin and Sulfa drugs. Smoker, 1 pack per day for 40 years. Labs from last week: FBS 165 mg/dL, HbA1c 8.1%, Cr 1.4 mg/dL, Na 138, K 3.4 mEq/L (low). Patient complains of persistent cough, increased shortness of breath, and occasional leg swelling.

expected_ddi.reason: SSRI + NSAID increases GI bleeding risk
Loop diuretics can impair renal function, increasing lactic acidosis risk
Additive hypotensive effect, risk of first-dose hypotension

expected_flags: Hypokalemia (K 3.4) with furosemide — needs potassium monitoring
NSAID use in elderly with possible renal impairment
COPD patient still smoking — cessation counseling needed
Symptoms suggest possible heart failure exacerbation
